sections.h2: Who sends the Pensacola tax bill
sections.html:
The envelope for a Pensacola address is mailed by the Escambia County tax collector, using a value supplied by the county property appraiser. Inside the city limits, one parcel can answer to several taxing bodies at once.

Among the bodies the collector bills for are the school board, the county commission, the City of Pensacola, the Town of Century, the Sheriff, the Downtown Improvement Board and the Northwest Florida Water Management District. A downtown house may carry a line that a house out in the county never sees. The collector's site searches by name, address or account number and shows the lines on your parcel.

The appraiser has no say over budgets, tax rates or special assessments. Rate complaints belong with whichever taxing body set the rate. Value or exemption questions go to escpa.org.

The city counted 54,312 residents in 2020, and household income has a median of $72,699 for 2019 to 2023. Naval Air Station Pensacola brings a steady flow of newcomers on military orders, which keeps a buyer pool coming even in slow months.

Location inside the city moves the bill. On the appraiser's millage page the Downtown Improvement Board stands as its own authority, and Pensacola Beach has a separate total. Look at the parcel record before pricing the house, since a Beach address and a downtown address are taxed differently.

Bills go out in November. For 2026 bills the collector shows a 4 percent discount through December 2, 2026, then 3 percent for the rest of that month, 2 percent in January 2027 and 1 percent in February 2027. The full amount is due in March 2027, and anything unpaid is delinquent on April 1, 2027.

The collector's notice on Amendment 3 says voters approved it on November 3, 2026. The vote leaves the 2026 bill alone, and new homestead exemption amounts begin with the 2027 tax year.

Escambia also offers a quarterly plan to taxpayers whose prior year taxes topped $100 and who have no mortgage escrow. Sign up by April 30 of the year you want to use it.

Quarterly plan terms

FirstJune 306%

Miss the June payment and you drop out for that year and get an ordinary November bill. The first two payments are a quarter of last year's tax each, and the last two split what is actually owed. The collector may also take a partial payment toward current taxes, without a discount, if an application comes in before April.

sections.h2: Exemptions a Pensacola homeowner can claim
sections.html:
Homestead is first on the list. The appraiser wants the application in before March 1. You qualify if you hold title, live in the home in good faith and make it your permanent home on January 1.

  • Homestead: $25,000 off every levy, plus up to $25,000 more on assessed value over $50,000 for levies other than school taxes.
  • Senior add-on: owners 65 by January 1 whose household adjusted gross income is under the yearly cap, printed as $38,686 for 2026. The county's $50,000 covers county taxes only, and a separate City of Pensacola $50,000 covers city taxes only.
  • Widow or widower: $5,000, supported by a death certificate.
  • Disability or blindness: $5,000, with proof from Social Security or a Florida physician.
  • Military service: $5,000 for a disability rated at ten percent or higher, and homestead relief for a total, permanent service-connected disability.

Save Our Homes holds yearly growth in a homestead's taxable value to the smaller of 3 percent or the Consumer Price Index change. The appraiser says that limit is lost on a sale, a rental or any change of ownership, and the next owner must apply fresh.

sections.h2: Who pays in the year of the sale
sections.html:
The closing agent usually settles the current year, with the title company doing the arithmetic. Request the parcel's payoff and ask which years are paid, open or delinquent.

Ask, too, how this year's bill will be shared with the buyer. An earlier year left unpaid may already have a tax certificate sold against it, so get the exact balance from the collector before signing. Owners who held the home as a homestead can ask the appraiser about portability, which lets the Save Our Homes benefit follow you to a new Florida homestead if you set it up within the allowed window, up to $500,000 of benefit.

Your buyer's first bill may look nothing like yours. After a sale the assessment is reset to market value, so an asking price pitched around your old tax figure can mislead. Point buyers to the appraiser's record instead.

  • Request a payoff figure from the collector.
  • Look up the deed history in the clerk's Official Records.
  • Tell the appraiser if you hold an exemption or classification that ends with the sale.

sections.h2: Where a Pensacola deed is recorded
sections.html:
Escambia's clerk of court maintains the Official Records; search them at escambiaclerk.com. Deed stamps run at seventy cents per $100 of price in every Florida county but Miami-Dade, and the Department of Revenue says the clerk collects the tax when a deed is recorded.

Once the deed is recorded, the appraiser changes the owner on the tax roll. Your homestead does not move with the new name, so a buyer planning to live there must apply on their own.

Before you list, gather four things: your latest bill, the exemption confirmation from the appraiser, the deed as recorded and any letter from the collector about open years. Having them in one folder lets the title agent start on day one.

Planning a fast sale, with an agent or to a cash buyer? Call the collector early. A written payoff holds for a stated date only, so you may need a fresh one if closing slips. Without a lender involved there is no loan review, but the title company still checks every tax year on the parcel.

A short list helps. Which years are paid? Is any certificate outstanding? What is the payoff if closing happens on a date you name? Are any special district charges on the parcel, and do they change with the sale? Write down the answers and the date, and keep the reply with your closing documents. If the answers are unclear, ask for them in writing and ask who at the office can confirm a figure for your closing date.

faqs.q: Does the city or the county send the Pensacola bill?
faqs.a: The county does. Escambia's tax collector issues it, and the City of Pensacola is one of several lines on it, next to the county, the school district and districts such as the Downtown Improvement Board.

faqs.q: When do Pensacola discounts begin and end?
faqs.a: They start with the November bill at 4 percent and step down monthly to 1 percent in February. For 2026 bills the collector shows 4 percent through December 2, 2026, with delinquency on April 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Can Pensacola owners split the bill into installments?
faqs.a: Yes, if last year's tax was over $100 and you have no escrow account. Apply by April 30; payments fall on June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31.

faqs.q: What does the senior exemption give in Pensacola?
faqs.a: It gives $50,000 off county taxes and a separate $50,000 off city taxes for owners past 65 under the income cap. The appraiser prints the 2026 cap as $38,686, with applications closing March 1.

faqs.q: Will a Pensacola sale change the taxable value?
faqs.a: Yes. A sale counts as a change of ownership, so the parcel is reassessed at market value and the new owner must apply for their own homestead before the Save Our Homes limit starts again.
